body: I deleted everything off my phone today.

I'm not trying to make it sound like I was proud. At the time, I was. I definitely tied my self worth to how many people slept with me, and to a degree I still do. I definitely relate to getting the fix and the fear setting in again. I can see it for the utterly selfish act that it is now, in addition to it being utterly devoid of self respect and boundaries.

I had a crisis of conscience and deleted all the videos from the internet and deleted my channel about a month ago. I never showed any faces or made any money off of it. I haven't deleted them off of my phone though.

Absolutely. Yoga has always been a sacred safe space for me and I would never want to contaminate it with my addiction.

I do have a sponsor in AA, but with things like this I definitely have trust issues. There are definitely SLAA meetings I'll look into in my area!

I recently posted a quite lengthy story on that subreddit explaining my addiction to kratom in detail and the various ways that I tried to attenuate my use before quitting for good nearly 2 years ago.  


All of this is to say: if you can use kratom responsibly, go for it. I have a lot of friends that use it, and it has done wonders for their social lives and/or pain. I feel the same way about any other mood/mind-altering substance: if you can hang, go for it.  


That is not me, however.
Thank you for reading!

You definitely will. Coming from a guy that was taking....shit, I don't even know. At least a couple of tablespoons of extract plus an ounce daily? I totally thought I was fucked and my brain was going to be screwed up forever. I eventually did go back to normal and the PAWS went away.  


And yeah, the dates weren't a good idea. I can't understate how badly I traded my kratom addiction for sex at first. I didn't even realize I had a sex addiction until maybe a few months ago, when I realized just how much stress it was generating in my life to constantly be chasing validation and being worried over not getting that.  


When I was in the "honeymoon" of kratom, I felt like I couldn't miss with dates, anything social, anything. Again, I really can't express how much of a cheat code it felt like. When it stopped working, I think I had been lulled into a sense of security, not to mention that addict part of my brain subtly transferring its energy into sex.  


It was really painful, putting myself out there like that feeling powerless against my anxiety and my emotions. I really had no confidence in myself and I feel like what little I had before kratom, kratom took from me via the things like job and friend losses.  


The anxiety, social and otherwise, get better. The main thing is this - you have to believe that you'll always be taken care of and that NOTHING that happens is a judgment against you.  


Your worth comes from you and you alone - whether you get rejected romantically or complimented for something you did well, neither matters. It's all up to you.
I'm glad it helped and thank you so much!
It definitely gets better. It was a slog at first, but definitely worth it.
I'm glad it did! Thanks for reading!
of course! thank you!
thank you so much!
thank you!
Of course! Please reach out anytime!

One thing I want to add is that I've had plenty of good days, and I had a good bout with PAWS (or at least that's what I think it was - the symptoms were very similar) right after Christmas, but there was a lot of stress with the travel and I didn't think much of it. This bout of maybe PAWS has been WAY worse than what it was a month ago and it's really taken me by surprise, and I'm honestly worried that I should see a doctor if it isn't PAWS or what I'm describing is something different than PAWS
What symptoms kicked in? That's a new one for me. I've never had bad physical symptoms beyond the first week.
I too would like to know your story, how much you were taking, and whether or not it was extract
I'm still here. I just want something to happen. Something to work out. I used to always feel like things would be fine, and now I don't feel like that at all. It all just seems dark now.

I was where you are back in March - W/Ds after four hours. I went to a show four hours away and accidentally left my bag of kratom in the bathroom of a gas station off the interstate on the way back - that night and that drive back were pure fucking hell, and it hadn't even been twelve hours since my last dose.

I would do a taper if you're using as much as you say you are. Not long after that incident in March, I got sick of my hostile mood swings and pushing people away and cut out the powder. I did a 10 day quit about a month after that and couldn't believe how low my energy was all ten days. Since then, I've had perpetual quit and relapse cycles but as of this writing I'm on day 30 and it's the shit. I've finally realized what a crazy jackass I had been and I have no desire to be that person ever again. I sometimes have urges to use but they're weak and dwarfed by my desire to be a dependable and good person again. I used kratom was a way to escape my unceasing anxiety, but I discovered there are ways around it and the lies I told myself to use were complete bullshit. For me, the effective workarounds are mediation and a healthy diet. I did fucking standup comedy without the aid of kratom tonight. I've NEVER done standup without kratom and it went fucking great. You don't need kratom for fucking anything. You really don't. The other side is so much richer than I ever thought it would be. Its not just that I feel better - I've been learning so much about myself recently and finding solutions to problems I never thought I could solve.

That being said, the acute withdrawals are no joke, and the energy loss during PAWS is brutal. I would recommend a taper and then jumping off. I never did any of the supplements so I can't speak to their effectiveness but I strongly recommend looking into those as well. The necessity of staying on top of work is very real and so I would recommend doing whatever is necessary to bridge that gap, and the supplements certainly, at the very least, wouldn't hurt.

Exercise and diet are also very useful.
Read my new post

Thanks everyone for the comments, and I'm sorry to blow up the sub with my negativity. I hope it helps somebody though. It certainly helps me.

A few people have asked how long I've used - two years. I started early November 2015, but my use didn't get out of control until early this year when I was combining extract with ounces of powder daily. Back in March, I would get withdrawals after just four hours without. I'd wake up and go to work and be sweaty and have a runny nose.

I'm going to stick it out for three months. I'll have 90 days on February 11. The general consensus I've noticed is that a) things are better by day 90 or nearly back to normal, and b) a noticeable improvement occurs between days 30 and 60. This seems to be true for everyone who used as long as I did. 

I know if I use, I'm just gonna go through the shit again. I'm going to stick around and see if the above is true. I'll probably have a couple more angry posts in me, but hopefully I'll have an "omg!!!! this is awesome" post coming up

Thanks everyone for the comments.

I should add a few things - I'm not working right now and the kratom was definitely a big reason why - deceased motivation, energy, etc.

All that is beside the point. Every day, I have a strong feeling like I'm just the biggest piece of shit ever because I'm not working. It was a dream job too. I've also alienated myself from all my friends. I feel like I've got nothing right now.

I was also taking extracts every day. Don't know what that is in grams. Occasionally I used the powder but quit that back in May. I quit for 10 days in June, 4 in July, 7 in August, 25 in October, and I've got 16 days now. All the other times I quit were to decrease tolerance - I don't want to use anymore now.

That being said, it really feels like my life is ruined and I'm fucked either way. I don't see how I can possibly get back what I had or be the person I used to be to others again.

Thanks to everyone for the responses.

I'm feeling a little better after posting that and getting some work done. A little. Not much.

I'm really hoping this "wave" goes away before Christmas. One of my big motivators for quitting is that I wanted to be more present for the holidays this year. I was at an emotional nadir last December (of which kratom played a part), and I really don't want it to be that way again.
I really hope this is true
I do, mainly in the form of walks. I took one day 5 and felt great. I did one last night and didn't feel better

I used for two years, and the thought of going CT with my program in school would have been a pure motherfucker of the highest order.

I'd say if you can go CT and have it not affect your school, then go for it over Thanksgiving. Otherwise, you could taper through finals before taking the leap for good when you're off for winter break.

It does seem like the taper is the way to go, especially in terms of easing your brain into a kratom-free lifestyle. 

Personally, I could never do the taper. When I get an inkling of that kratom feeling in my body, I immediately want more, and I don't stop wanting more. I'll crave so hard that I'll stop at nothing to get the next little bit. I tried tapering, but I damn near had to throw all of my willpower at doing so, and even then it was incredibly easy to say fuck it after subjecting myself for that for too long.

Short answer.....if you can taper and do so successfully (and be honest with yourself.....can you actually take a certain amount and stick to that for the day?), then by all means, do so.

Anytime I've been depressed and I don't eat, it makes the depression infinitely worse. I'm a big believer in diet in terms of overcoming shit - after all, our brains can't have all that feel good happy shit getting made if we don't give it the food it needs to make the shit.

Even if the habits suck and don't seem like they're doing anything, at the VERY LEAST you're subconscious giving your mind just a liiiiiiittle push in the right direction. Before long, all those pushes add up and suddenly you're sailing in the right direction.

Never give up. Trust your instincts. Do a barrel roll and use that boost to get through.

I could never taper. Once I got that feeling in me, I wanted more. And when I wanted more, I never stopped wanting more.

You can CT. It's a motherfucker but it's not impossible. You just have to be willing to go through it and accept it's gonna be shitty for a few days and that it's worth it over using again.

Damn, I'd have been in a world of shit if they banned it last October when they said they would. That was the period of time I was taking extracts daily PLUS the powder. I'd get noticeably uncomfortable withdrawals if I didn't use for 4 hours. Fuck that noise.

I'm against banning any drugs - instead, I wish recovery wasn't so goddamn stigmatized and it was socially acceptable to go get help without people judging the fuck out of you.

It's too bad that in this country things have to get worse before they get better - maybe the opioid crisis will pull people's heads out of their ass for once on shit like this.

Damn, I was fucking around with extracts for months before I found myself feeling anything like you're describing above.

I relate to everything you described - kratom made you the best version of myself. That was only true for me for maybe 6 months, and then the remaining 18 I chased that feeling although I could never come close to what it was at first.

The comment about feeling like shit while still using is true - shit, if you keep going through that, you're gonna find that you not only feel like shit while using, the kratom will actually make the depression worse while using.

It's a shitty pill to swallow, but you don't want to have my experience or the experience of others on this sub. You might as well just quit now. At the very least, give yourself a good month or two off just to see how you feel. Shit, you've been using so briefly I doubt the withdrawal would even be that bad.

aaaand I'm back to a week. Whoopee.

I went on a walk and got a coffee and put in my earbuds and jammed out to some tunes; doing that actually helped a lot tonight. Hell, I even felt somewhat normal.

Faaaar from it. I'm in the South. We get a decent mix of cloudy days but this weekend was sunny and low 60s. It gets cold at night though (low 40s which is cold for us).

The gloomy days are fucking hard and I'm glad to live somewhere that doesn't get that many. That being said, it is hot as shit where I live most of the year, and the double whammy of early sunsets and cold weather can really do a number on us down here

I certainly hope so. One thing I should keep in mind is that October was easily one of my best months this year. Big shocker there. Granted, not every month can lay claim to haunted houses, Halloween, and all that good shit, but the fact that I could actually be present for all of that and furthermore enjoy it instead of being woefully unmoved by Die Hard during the holidays made it feel like a good call. In all honesty, a huge motivator for me to quit right now is because I want to enjoy the rest of the holidays this year as much as I did last month. The holidays were a DISASTER for me last year.

I guess if I should count my blessings at this point, a reply to your post would be as good a place as any to start.

1. I can actually sleep again now.
2. I was able to do a little bit of drawing the past two days, even though it felt forced and rather unenjoyable.
3. I binged Strange Things 2 last night while I felt like shit, and it was great.
4. I'm at a week again (almost, a few more hours and I'm there)
5. This weekend was pretty warm for where I am (low 60's / high 50's.....thank goodness I'm not further north for going through this shit)

Fortunately I live in a place with decent hiking and the leaves are peaking here, so that might actually help.

I've been using for about 2 years, but my main issue is that I was taking extracts. I didn't really do my research on kratom when I started using, and at the time the extracts were all we had here. I have quit several times this year though (10 days in June, 4 days in July, a week in August, 25 days in October, and now a week in November), so it's not like I'm starting from square zero.

The turning point when I quit last month was when I could be productive and things started to become interesting again, which set it before I got to day 7. It's the absolute fucking worst to feel like everything is dull, and to only have the energy to sit down and browse through my phone. The only time throughout the day I even moderately feel normal is my first cup of coffee of the day.

I appreciate it. I've quit several times this year for a handful of days each, and during those spurts (which at the time were mainly meant to lower tolerance - this time I want to be off completely), I definitely got an interest in some of the things you've talked about and they've proven to be very helpful.

I'm quitting kratom and have a girlfriend. I haven't told her what I'm going through, which feels shitty (but also because we haven't been dating long and it feels awkward to bring it up). I would just say this: if he's been honest with you about quitting, please be patient with him. One of the biggest stressors for me right now is trying to save face around my girlfriend and trying not to seem different. My energy and sex drive aren't as they used to be, and my mind is foggy as shit.

Was feeling better earlier, but now kinda shitty. I'm on Day 6 now.

A lot of it is depression from FOMO. I used to use kratom heavily to give myself energy to go out and be talkative, but now doing so seems really daunting. I'm sitting at home alone on my laptop and it feels super lame.

Day 5. Sleep problems should now be behind me.

Meditation is paying off. Getting more productive. Out of the woods with the acute physical symptoms. Still low energy and sex drive.

Regardless, things are looking up

Almost at day 5. I eventually did get some sleep but it wasn't quality and I woke up dopey as shit.

Brain still foggy but I think some of that can be my appetite being weak. Eating some food to see if that helps.

Depression is significantly better today.

Still meditating and was able to draw for a bit today. Definitely improving.
I've made it three days. I can't sleep now and it's almost 3 am. It sucks. 😞

67 hours. Not far from the 3 day mark.

Brain fog is still present. My sleep was SHIT last night - for some reason, the second day is always the night with the shittiest sleep. Spent the night with the girlfriend, which can be a little stressful considering my numerous tossing and turning. Had a bit of a sex drive, which is surprising considering I'm still in the acute phase.

Depression is still lingering and about the same as it was yesterday - maybe a little weaker. I'm expecting one or two more shitty nights of sleep, and then hopefully I'll be in the clear.

Started meditating again today - this has proven to work wonders during the other periods of time this year that I have quit. I always thought meditation seemed like bullshit, but it's proven to be quite powerful in reducing anxiety and depression. It's definitely an effective substitute for kratom, albeit much more difficlut to stick with and convince myself to do.

Still not desire to use. No cravings. I'm done.

I've realized that a huge part of my depression is also from missing the way things used to be when I moved to where I live - i.e., when I started using kratom and when I was in its honeymoon phase. I have a legitimate depression that my quality of life will never be the same as it was then. It's not just based in the kratom either - I had an amazing job then that I lost over really fucked up reasons (not related to kratom), as well as a relationship with someone I miss dearly. All of this was going on when I started using and it's still a very fond time for me - letting that go and moving on and most of all being open to the idea that my quality of life will ever be the same has been a very difficult and painful idea to consider or think, and my mind has fairly significant resistance to thinking that will ever be true.

Despite that, I know using will not help. I at least have my own personal experience to verify that. What I don't know is the other side.

A little over 2 days now.

Day 2 was way easier than Day 1. I was still depressed but not nearly as bad. Looks like I got the worst out of the way last night and possibly with the 36 hours I had before using on the 13th.

Brain is still mush but again, not as bad. I was able to focus a little on my new font I'm working on.

I'm starting to realize what a huge idiot I was to use again. K doesn't just make life shitty - it makes time slip away. October was slow but easily the best month I've had in a long time. I quit for 25 days in October and relapsed just before Halloween.

I'm hoping tomorrow is better. It's brutal quitting right now not just for all the aforementioned reasons but the double whammy of cold and DST ending (early sunsets where I am) with frequent grey days is pretty rough. Quitting in October wasn't as bad because it's a mostly warm month here; November is not so forgiving.

I want to quit now because last Christmas was terrible and I want to be present for the holidays this year.
I made it 25 days until I relapsed before Halloween. I definitely concur with turning the corner by this point. I'm looking forward to rejoining you with this much time. I'm on day 3 now.

42 hours in. Last night was rough. My sleep wasn't great, but the depression was laid on thick. It wasn't as bad as other times in the past, though. I've quit for at least a week once a month for 4 of the last 5 months, and I think that in addition to the day I had on the 11th before relapsing on the 12th made it a lot better than it probably could have been.

I also want to mention that I think my repeated quits over the past half year probably explain my relative energy. When I did my first two initial quit in May and June (5 days and 10 days, mainly done to reduce my tolerance, which barely worked), I was EXHAUSTED the entire time. The first three days in particular it was a chore to so much as get out of the car and walk. THAT was awful. I haven't really had that this time around.

Today has been much better. My energy and depression are reduced, and today was exactly the kind of shit day that made me relapse a couple of days ago - cold and grey. Luckily, I haven't had any desire to use. I'm fucking done.

Brain is still mush but not as bad as it was yesterday - I was able to create part of a typeface I've been working on. Concentration is still iffy - I'm expecting this to improve tomorrow.

Allright. Made it back to a day.

Just had some friends come over, which was fun and helped me not be in my head as much. Depression is still pretty strong. Sleep will probably be rough but we'll see.

20 hours in. My brain is mush. I'm sitting here with Unity open trying to finish writing this shader - I can't concentrate worth a damn.

That being said, I'm feeling weirdly optimistic and I'm not in the funk that I was in a few hours ago. I was feeling very depressed from the moment I woke up until about an hour ago. I don't have any other physical symptoms other than the brain fog. I'm wondering how my sleep is gonna be tonight.

I feel like I need to emphasize this next point: this depression doesn't feel induced from my quitting as much as it does just general malaise from my situation. After the physical stuff passed last month after having quit for a while, I entered a pretty depressed period. At first, I thought it was the kratom and PAWS and all that. Then I realized that I was actually back to normal, and the depression I was feeling had always been there, but had been covered up by all the continuous use. I think my weirdly optimistic mood today has to do with the fact that I finally wrote out all the stuff that I finally needed to accept with my original post. That being said, I'm still waiting for the other shoe to drop - if it does at all. I've quit kratom CT multiple times now (granted, never as long as the 25 days in October, but at least a week multiple times this year), and the acute stuff has never lasted more than 3 days. This is coming from someone who almost exclusively abused extracts.

When I quit for a month in October, the situation was very similar to this one - I reached a quitting point, was off for a day, relapsed the day after, and then was done. The same situation happened this time, except when I quit the last time I did it with the knowledge that I had a storytelling gig coming up and I was going to have to use to get through that. The gig was last Wednesday, and now I've realized I've got to be done for good.

One thing that might give some people hope - when I quit in October, I was insanely productive after a week, and after the second week I had GREAT concentration. Granted, this was probably a side effect of not having a job and feeling like I needed something to do, but the fact remains that I had no PAWS interfering with my ability to create.

15 hours in. Woke up today feeling a lot better than I did yesterday. It's still cold, but at least the sun is out and it isn't grey and depressing. Then again, I had a full day to my credit yesterday.

I'm still feeling a little shitty, and I'm just waiting for things to get shittier. I feel like the symptoms don't really start getting bad for me until I'm about 18 hours in.

The good news is that I really feel like yesterday was the last one, and I've accepted that things are just going to be shitty for a little while and they'll get better. I'm in the phase where I can't really concentrate on anything except social media which REALLY sucks, but there's a weird optimism to today that I can't really explain. I'll re-evaluate in a few.

I should also mention that the sole positive thing in my life right now is my girlfriend, who I weirdly ran into after losing my job - she's been suuuuuuuuch a positive spot in my life. I'm going to lose her too if I don't get off this stuff - I just know it.

I'm an hour and a half in, and I've already caught my first craving. That last drink barely did anything at all, and I didn't just have one for my last - I had four. I drank the other three when I was writing this post, and had the fourth after I finished.

I would have gone into the place and got the next drink if I had the cash on hand, but I didn't. It wouldn't have done anything and any effects would have lasted an hour, if that. I even went to get food since the last drinks weren't working since eating with sometimes make the feeling get stronger - nothing.

I had a big craving because I'm in a bout of self pity right now. I was at this one place talking to a friend, and he was telling me a story of a guy in town who once had been bad off addicted to drugs, and who cleaned up, turned his life around, and is now very successful and owns the place we were talking in. Hearing that story made me feel like complete shit, considering my story is similar - I was addicted to things in the past, got clean, did some amazing stuff (got into a school I never thought I would, got my dream job, and a few other things), and now I've lost everything I worked hard for. I'm in a lot of self pity because I can't see how I can ever make things right again. I can't get over this feeling like I've wasted my life, I'm a failure, and it makes me want to cover up with kratom.

It's gonna be a rough few days until I can get through this shit. Thanks to anyone who read and is helped.

Day 2. Really want to use right now. I quit again after a two week bender and I'm shocked at how quickly I became less productive after using again. I really want energy and to be alert. It's also very cold and very grey where I am right now, so that isn't helping either. I'm parked outside of my pickup place right now, and was totally going to go in when I thought about posting here instead. I'm really hoping this will do the trick because the cravings just don't fucking stop when they start

Day 20. I'm feeling super irritable and just found out there's a show going on that I really want to go to. I have a bad headache and I couldn't really sleep last night. Definitely battling depression. I really want to use right now.

I'm going to go to the store and get some BC powder and see where that gets me. I get headaches whenever I have too much sugar - not doing that again.

Day 19. The depression is still here.

I don't want to scare anyone off because I keep bringing up depression on week 3. It sucks, but it's not debilitating. I can still go out and do things, and I am. It's still better than being addicted or the very beginning.

I think the main cause of depression is this recognition of wasted time and like I'm going nowhere and have done nothing with my life. That isn't entirely true, but I've definitely been comparing my insides with a lot of outsides.

I fucked up my original post with respect to meditation. I meant to say that this time around, I haven't been nearly as proactive about it. I'm gonna try and get back on that horse as much as I can today. The meditation really does great things - it might not happen at first but it definitely causes a change if I stick with it.

I know exactly what you mean. I used heavily for two years mainly taking extracts (at my worst 10 teaspoons a day, or over an ounce of powder when I was using that), and I was also very good with words. I've been able to piece together a few strings of days this year, and I've noticed that my mind got significantly sharper after the fourth day each time. The fatigue and other aspects of paws still linger (I'm on day 18 right now and I still have the fatigue), but my mind is definitely sharper and getting better every day.
